affectedPublicSurfaces: THE PREDICATE FUNCTION ITSELF — a new pure function at `services/agent/workflows/process_order/predicate.py` taking one order's facts and returning one verdict: `clean`, or excluded with EXACTLY ONE named reason. There is NO HTTP surface in this slice: no route, no response model, no write, no I/O of any kind. That is what makes it releasable ahead of everything that consumes it, and it is also why the only honest post-deploy evidence is that NOTHING on any live surface moved.

THE EXCLUSION VOCABULARY, which becomes a contract the moment anything reads it. The full set the predicate must cover: not awaiting shipment; still inside the one-hour `ON_HOLD` remorse window; fulfilled by TikTok; own carrier; CANCELLATION PENDING; address updated since the order was read; no stock on the system bucket; ship error or abnormal package state. Every reason is reachable, and an excluded order carries exactly one — never two, never a generic 'not clean'. #1799's card, #1801's payload and #1805's digest all render these strings, so an enum invented loosely here is an enum three later slices are stuck with.

THE CANCELLATION EXCLUSION IS A HARD EXCLUSION IN JULI'S OWN CODE. ADR-092's 2026-09-05 amendment (research/dispatch-sla-batch-exceptions.md) records that TikTok does NOT refuse a ship write while a cancellation request is pending: the write goes through, the cancellation is approved anyway, and the seller pulls a parcel back off the courier pile. The on-disk ADR Context and `seller-journeys/process-order-actors.md` §E row 3 still describe the vendor refusal as a backstop — they are SUPERSEDED. No branch anywhere in this module may defer the decision to a vendor refusal, and that absence is asserted, not assumed.

THE DEADLINE LADDER AND THE RECORDED RUNG — `rts_sla_time`, else `tts_sla_time`, else `collection_due_time`, else the documented cutoff (14:00, two working days) as the LAST RESORT, with the rung it came from recorded beside the deadline. The rung is the honesty mechanism: a run built on a guessed cutoff must stay distinguishable from one built on observed vendor fields in every later reading, and #1805's measure reads that rung rather than a constant. Nothing like this exists today — `services/aggregates/thresholds.py:11` holds a GLOBAL `ORDER_DISPATCH_SLA_HOURS = 48` off `payment_time`, which `computed_kpis.py:136-153` measures against, and no `*_sla_time` field appears in any live capture (PO-NFR-1). This slice does not touch that constant or that KPI; it introduces the ladder beside them.

THE SORT KEY. Clean orders sort by their RESOLVED DEADLINE, not by `payment_time` and not by the 48-hour proxy. Moving one order's `rts_sla_time` past another's reverses the pair — that is the observable difference between the ladder and the constant.

NO schema change, NO route, NO write, NO vendor call, NO card. The facts arrive from the silver columns and order-scoped signals #1796 adds plus the order read itself; the function performs no I/O whatsoever.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE IN THIS SLICE. Every fact the predicate reads — the raw TikTok order status on silver, the per-order cancellation-pending record, the order-scoped signal rows — is created by #1796 and is a HARD DEPENDENCY, not something to add here. Do not open a migration file and do not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`. If a test cannot pass without a column, the dependency on #1796 is unmet and the answer is to REPORT IT, not to write a second migration; two migrations for one column is exactly how this tree ended up with two same-numbered `043_*` files. Stable and candidate run the same schema, so they are trivially compatible and a code rollback needs no downgrade. Recording the rung on a run row, or persisting a verdict, is #1799/#1805 work with its own reserved number.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. There is no predicate, so nothing selects orders for dispatch and nothing downstream can be built; #1799's producer stays blocked. The deployed system is unchanged — the 48-hour constant keeps driving `computed_kpis.py` exactly as it does today, and no seller sees anything different. A failing predicate must never be merged 'to unblock #1799': a wrong verdict here becomes a wrongly shipped or wrongly withheld parcel three slices later.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. NO DOWNGRADE IS NEEDED OR POSSIBLE — there is no migration, no persisted state and no row written by this slice. Because the function has no caller yet, removing it cannot strand a run, cannot orphan a card and cannot leave a half-shipped batch: the rollback is a code swap and nothing else. If a later slice is already deployed on top, roll that back FIRST, since #1799's producer and #1803's re-verify both import this module and would fail to import without it.

doNotInfer: Do NOT write a migration. This slice has NO schema change; every column it reads comes from #1796. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META and never read from head — but the correct action here is not to reserve one, it is to not need one.

Do NOT build a vendor-refusal branch, and do NOT write a comment or a test that treats the vendor as a backstop. ADR-092's 2026-09-05 amendment: TikTok does NOT refuse a ship write during a pending cancellation — the write succeeds and the cancellation is approved anyway. The exclusion is HARD, in Juli's own code, at selection and again at re-verify. The on-disk ADR Context and `seller-journeys/process-order-actors.md` §E row 3 still say the opposite; they are superseded.
Do NOT propose, request or imply a cancellation for any order. The predicate EXCLUDES an order; it never cancels one, and no cancel tool exists in this allowlist, ever.

Do NOT recompute a cutoff when the order carries a deadline field. The ladder is `rts_sla_time` → `tts_sla_time` → `collection_due_time`, and the documented cutoff (14:00, two working days) is the LAST RESORT ONLY, taken when all three are absent and recorded as the fallback rung.

Do NOT reuse `ORDER_DISPATCH_SLA_HOURS = 48` (`services/aggregates/thresholds.py:11`) or `payment_time` as the deadline, and do NOT edit that constant or `computed_kpis.py:136-153`. Replacing the measure is #1805; this slice introduces the ladder beside the proxy.
Do NOT perform I/O in the predicate — no session, no HTTP client, no repository call. Facts in, verdict out. It is re-run at re-verify (#1803) and must be cheap and side-effect-free.
Do NOT emit a card, group a batch into buckets, build a window, or write anything. Those are #1799 and later.
Do NOT return more than one reason for an excluded order, and do NOT return a generic 'not clean'. Three downstream slices render these strings to sellers.
Do NOT add FBT or Seller Own Fleet handling beyond EXCLUDING them with their named reasons. FBT is monitor-only by design (`21008025` — the vendor refuses the write) and own-carrier is v2.

Do NOT add a Create Packages or a Confirm Package Shipment path: in SEA TikTok creates the package at order time, and Confirm Package Shipment is certified-warehouse-provider-only (ADR-092 Context defects 1 and 2).

Do NOT hand-build the order objects the tests use. Bind to the REAL order object built from the #1719 awaiting-shipment capture; a `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real object carries the field the predicate reads.
Do NOT touch ETL, migrations, the vendor client or any `/v1` route — one domain per issue.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/**, which are on this epic's doNotLoad list.
